name: 红崖口
Red Cliff Gate
before: 出了龙尾门往东北走三天，戈壁尽头忽然立起一道红崖，崖面上密密麻麻全是窟口，像一面被虫蛀空的蜂巢。崖下一溜胡杨，叶子黄得发亮。路口横着一道木栅，一队戴金面具的刀卫和弩手守着，面具在太阳底下晃眼。领头的敲着栅栏喊：「千佛洞闭山十年，香客、商人、和尚，一概回去！」

Three days north-east of the Dragon's Tail Gate, a red cliff rises out of the end of the gravel plain, its face riddled with cave mouths like a honeycomb eaten hollow. Below it runs a line of desert poplars, their leaves a shining yellow. A wooden barrier blocks the road, held by swordsmen and crossbowmen in golden masks that flash in the sun. Their leader raps on the bars: 'The Thousand Buddha Caves have been closed for ten years. Pilgrims, merchants, monks: all of you, turn back!'
after: 金面卫退进了胡杨林。木栅上钉着一块旧木牌：「闭山令。洞主无相。」牌子底下有人用炭写了一行小字：「了账到此，进不去，在山门坡等你们。」风从崖上吹下来，带着香灰和旧颜料的味道。千里号三百人，十年前就是从这道口子走进去的。

The Gold Masks fall back into the poplars. Nailed to the barrier is an old board: 'The mountain is closed. By order of the Lord of the Caves, Wuxiang.' Beneath it someone has scrawled in charcoal: 'Liaozhang was here. Couldn't get in. Waiting for you at Temple Gate Slope.' The wind off the cliff smells of incense ash and old paint. Ten years ago the Qianli caravan's three hundred walked in through this very gap.

name: 卖脸摊
The Face Stall
before: 路边一顶布棚，挂满了巴掌大的泥皮，每片泥皮上是半张人脸：一只眼、一截鼻梁，颜色里闪着细细的金星。摊主吆喝：「千里号的金脸，贴门上辟邪，一片五钱！」几个假和尚模样的打手守着摊子，谁多问一句来路，就把谁推出去。有个老汉买了一片，对着太阳看了半天，说这只眼睛他认得。

A cloth awning by the road is hung with palm-sized flakes of plaster, each bearing part of a human face: an eye, the bridge of a nose, the paint flecked with tiny points of gold. 'Golden faces of the Qianli caravan!' the stallholder cries. 'Stick one on your door against evil, five coins a piece!' Toughs dressed as monks guard the stall and shove away anyone who asks where the faces came from. An old man buys one, squints at it against the sun, and says he knows that eye.
after: 打手一跑，摊主也溜了，只落下一片泥皮。上面的脸只剩半边，眉毛很粗，旁边题着一行墨字：「驼户曹三」。金星原来是调在颜料里的金粉。老汉说，十年前千佛洞的窟里画过三百个商人，后来不知被谁把脸全刮了，刮下来的渣子就流到了这种摊上。

The toughs bolt, the stallholder slips away, and one flake is left behind: half a face with heavy eyebrows, and beside it in ink, 'Cao San, camel driver.' The gold is gold dust mixed into the paint. Ten years ago, the old man says, three hundred merchants were painted in one of the caves. Later someone scraped every face off, and the scrapings ended up on stalls like this.

name: 描红塾
The Tracing School
before: 村口一间土坯学堂，十几个娃娃趴在桌上描红，描的不是字，是一张人脸：圆脸，笑眼，嘴边一颗痣。原稿是一张发黄的厚纸，线条上扎满了针眼。一伙逃兵占了学堂后院当营房，嫌娃娃吵，要把桌子劈了烧火。先生拿着戒尺挡在门口，手直哆嗦。

In a mud-brick schoolhouse at the edge of a village, a dozen children bend over their desks tracing, not characters, but a face: round, laughing eyes, a mole by the mouth. The original is a sheet of yellowed paper whose every line is pricked with pinholes. Deserters have taken over the back yard as a barracks; the children annoy them, and they mean to chop up the desks for firewood. The teacher stands in the doorway with his ruler, his hand shaking.
after: 逃兵被赶出了村，先生把那张原稿捧给你们看：针眼是画匠「拍粉」用的，炭粉拍过针眼，线就印到墙上，这叫粉本。纸角写着「千里号·伙夫老杨·第四十一」。「这是半壁村吴画匠的东西，」先生说，「娃娃们描了三年，描得比我还像老杨。」

With the deserters run out of the village, the teacher shows you the original. The pinholes are for pouncing: tap charcoal dust through them and the line transfers onto a wall. Painters call it a pounce pattern. In the corner: 'Qianli caravan. Old Yang, cook. No. 41.' 'It belonged to Wu the painter, from Half Wall village,' the teacher says. 'Three years of tracing, and the children draw Old Yang better than I do.'

name: 刮金龛
The Scraped Shrine
before: 一座路边小佛龛被围住了，五六个人拿着竹片，一下一下刮佛像脸上的金。他们自称「刮金帮」，刮了七八年，沿路的佛像个个成了灰脸。领头的是个缺牙老头，一边刮一边吹：「刮金算什么？千里号那三百张金脸，是戴金面具的人刮的，我亲眼看见的！」

A wayside shrine is surrounded by half a dozen men with bamboo slivers, scraping the gilt off the Buddha's face stroke by stroke. They call themselves the Gold Scrapers, and in seven or eight years every Buddha along this road has gone grey-faced. Their leader, a gap-toothed old man, brags as he works: 'This is nothing. The three hundred golden faces of the Qianli caravan? Men in golden masks scraped those. I saw it with my own eyes!'
after: 刮金帮四散，老头被你们按在龛前，把那晚的事又讲了一遍：月黑夜，一群戴金面具的人进了窟，叮叮当当刮到天亮，「金面卫，错不了」。可他说着说着又改口，说那些面具「好像是纸糊的，刷了金漆」。你们把他的话记了下来。

The Scrapers scatter, and you pin the old man in front of the shrine to tell it again. A moonless night, a band in golden masks went into the cave and scraped away until dawn. 'The Gold Masks. No mistake.' But halfway through he changes his tune: the masks 'looked like paper, now I think of it, painted gold'. You write down what he said.

name: 收脸车
The Face Collector's Cart
before: 一辆蒙着油布的大车，前后跟着一队关内来的镖师，刀都是新磨的。车上的掌柜是个收古董的胖子，专收千里号的「金脸」，一路收了十七片，用丝绵包着，要运回关内卖给大户人家，「千里号三个字，比金子值钱」。镖师们见你们打着旗，先把弓拉开了。

A big cart under oilcloth, escorted fore and aft by guards from inside the Pass, their blades freshly ground. Riding in it is a fat antiques dealer who collects nothing but the Qianli caravan's 'golden faces'. He has seventeen so far, wrapped in silk floss, bound for the great houses back home. 'The name Qianli is worth more than gold.' Seeing your banner, the guards draw their bows first.
after: 镖师们丢下车跑了，胖掌柜抱着他那箱泥皮直叹气。他倒是把账算得清：三百张脸的金粉加在一起，刮下来也不过一钱多，「不够打一只戒指」。值钱的从来不是金，是名声。十七片泥皮你们收下了，没有一片拼得上另一片。

The guards abandon the cart and the fat dealer sighs over his box of plaster. He has done the sums, at least: the gold dust in all three hundred faces, scraped together, comes to barely a tenth of an ounce. 'Not enough for a ring.' It was never the gold that was worth anything, only the name. You take the seventeen flakes. Not one of them fits against another.

name: 放羊坡
Shepherdess Slope
before: 坡上一个放羊的姑娘，十年来都在这片坡上放羊，离千佛洞的北崖不远。她到处跟人讲那天夜里看见的事，几个金面骑卫找上门来，说她「造谣惑众」，要把她带回山上问话。姑娘把鞭子一甩，站在羊群中间不肯走：「我看见的就是看见的！」

A girl has grazed her sheep on this slope, not far from the caves' north cliff, for ten years. She tells everyone what she saw one night, and now a few Gold Mask riders have come to take her up the mountain for 'spreading rumours'. She cracks her whip and plants herself among her sheep: 'What I saw, I saw!'
after: 金面骑卫被打回了山，姑娘这才把话说完：那夜月亮很亮，她赶夜路回家，看见北崖一个窟口里往外飘东西，一阵一阵，亮晶晶的，像下雪，「是脸自己掉下来了」。说完她自己打了个寒战。你们想起刮金帮的话：那一夜到底是有月亮，还是没月亮？

Once the riders are driven back up the mountain, she finishes her story. The moon was bright that night. Walking home late, she saw something drifting out of a cave mouth on the north cliff, gust after gust, glittering like snow. 'The faces fell off by themselves.' She shivers as she says it. You think of the Gold Scraper's version: was that night moonlit or moonless?

name: 半壁村
Half Wall Village
before: 半壁村只剩半堵墙，墙上画着半幅飞天，另外半幅没画完。吴画匠的家就在墙下，院里晒着一排排空颜料碟。一伙流民占了他家的西屋，把画笔拿来剔牙，把颜料碟摞起来当凳子。吴画匠的老伴吴婶攥着擀面杖守在灶房门口，一步不让。

All that's left of Half Wall village is half a wall, with half a flying apsara painted on it; the other half was never finished. Wu the painter's house sits beneath it, rows of empty paint dishes drying in the yard. Vagrants have taken the west room, picking their teeth with his brushes and stacking his dishes into stools. His wife, Aunt Wu, guards the kitchen door with a rolling pin and won't give an inch.
after: 流民被撵走，吴婶给你们烧了一锅茶。她说老吴给千里号画了三百个供养人，画了一冬天，一人一张脸。几年后脸被刮了，他连夜收拾了颜料担子出门，说「不把三百张脸补回来不回家」，一走七年。家里那捆三百页的粉本，早被一个货郎偷去卖了。

The vagrants chased off, Aunt Wu brews you a pot of tea. Old Wu painted the Qianli caravan's three hundred as donors, she says, a whole winter's work, one face for each. A few years later the faces were scraped. He packed his paints that same night and left, saying he wouldn't come home until all three hundred were back. That was seven years ago. The bundle of three hundred pounce patterns he kept at home was stolen and sold by a peddler long since.

name: 蝙蝠塔
Bat Pagoda
before: 戈壁上一座塌了顶的土塔，塔肚子里住满了蝙蝠，太阳一落山就黑压压地涌出来，遮住半边天。附近的人说这塔闹鬼，谁也不敢靠近。你们点着火把进去，蝙蝠扑面而来，翅膀扇得火苗乱窜。塔壁上隐约有炭笔画的东西，一层一层，被蝙蝠粪盖住了一半。

A roofless earthen pagoda stands on the gravel plain, its belly packed with bats that pour out at sunset in a cloud that blots out half the sky. Locals say it's haunted and keep away. You go in with torches and the bats come at your faces, their wings whipping the flames about. On the inner walls something is drawn in charcoal, layer on layer, half buried under droppings.
after: 这一回的蝙蝠被烟熏了出去。你们刮掉塔壁上的粪，底下是几十张炭笔画的人脸，个个画得飞快，旁边写着「怕忘」两个字，是吴画匠当年躲雨时凭记忆画的。可蝙蝠认这座塔，赶走了，过几天又飞回来，粪又一层层盖上去，只能隔一阵来清一回。

This lot of bats is smoked out. Scraping the droppings off the walls, you find dozens of charcoal faces, all drawn at speed, and beside them two words: 'Afraid I'll forget.' Wu the painter drew them from memory once, sheltering from the rain. But the bats know this pagoda. Drive them out and in a few days they're back, burying the faces again. Someone will have to come and clear it every so often.

name: 照壁店
The Painted Tavern
before: 一家酒店的照壁上画着一长溜供养人，个个手捧香炉，衣冠楚楚，可脸全是附近的熟面孔：卖油的老王、店主的丈母娘、村口的二傻子。店主说这是吴画匠当年拿来抵酒钱的，「画的是千里号，脸是他喝醉了随手抓的」。如今一伙兵痞占了酒店，喝光了酒，要店主把照壁上的人脸都改成他们自己。

The screen wall of a tavern carries a long row of donors in fine robes, each holding a censer, and every face is a local one: Wang the oil seller, the landlord's mother-in-law, the village simpleton. Wu the painter did it to settle his bar bill, the landlord says: 'The Qianli caravan, in theory. The faces were whoever he grabbed while drunk.' Now a gang of soldiers-turned-thugs has taken the tavern, drunk it dry, and wants every face on the wall changed to theirs.
after: 兵痞被打出了门，店主请你们喝了一碗剩下的酒。他说吴画匠酒后吹过牛：三百张脸他都记在脑子里，不用粉本也画得出来，「只是缺颜色。好颜色贵，金粉更贵」。照壁上的丈母娘看着你们，笑得很威严。

The thugs thrown out, the landlord pours you the last of the wine. Wu used to boast in his cups that he had all three hundred faces in his head and could paint them without any patterns. 'All he lacked was colour. Good colour costs, gold dust more.' On the wall, the mother-in-law regards you with a stern smile.

name: 搜面道
The Search Road
before: 一小队金面骑卫拦在路上，挨个搜过路人的包袱。搜的不是钱，是泥皮：凡是带着画了人脸的泥皮、纸片的，一律收走，一个铜子儿也不赔。一个货郎被搜出两片「金脸」，正跪在地上求饶。骑卫的面具在阳光下一晃一晃，看不出喜怒。

A small troop of Gold Mask riders blocks the road, searching every traveller's bundle. Not for money, for plaster: any flake or scrap of paper with a face on it is confiscated, not a copper paid. A peddler caught with two 'golden faces' is on his knees begging. The riders' masks glint in the sun and show nothing at all.
after: 骑卫们退了，丢下一只皮口袋，里面是一路收来的泥皮，每片都用纸包好，纸上写着收的日子和地方。口袋里还有一道令：「千里号残面，一片不许流出，收回入库。洞主无相。」原来金面卫满世界收的，就是那三百张脸。

The riders withdraw and leave behind a leather bag of plaster flakes collected along the road, each wrapped in paper marked with where and when. In the bag is an order: 'Not one fragment of the Qianli faces is to leave. All to be recovered and stored. Wuxiang, Lord of the Caves.' So that's what the Gold Masks have been gathering up all over the country: the three hundred faces.

name: 换脸沟
Fake Face Gully
before: 沟里搭着一溜棚子，棚里坐着几个画匠，正往旧墙皮上画脸，画好了用烟熏黄，再撒一把铜粉冒充金星，就成了「千里号原件」。领头的是吴画匠早年的徒弟，雇了一帮打手看棚子。你们进沟的时候，他正照着一个过路人的脸画，画完还收了人家十个钱。

A row of sheds lines the gully, and in them painters dab faces onto old wall plaster, smoke them yellow, sprinkle on brass filings for gold, and call them 'genuine Qianli'. The man in charge was once Wu the painter's apprentice, and he's hired toughs to mind the sheds. When you arrive he is painting a passing traveller's face, and charging him ten coins for the privilege.
after: 打手散了，那徒弟跪下认了错。他说真粉本印上墙的线是一串细点，假的都是一笔画成，一看就破。他还说七年前见过师父一面，师父挑着颜料担子往东去了，要去南边山里找「能画脸的红、能画衣的绿」。「师父那人，说找就找一辈子。」

The toughs gone, the apprentice kneels and owns up. A true pounce pattern leaves a line of fine dots on the wall; fakes are drawn in one stroke and give themselves away at a glance. Seven years ago, he says, he saw his master once, heading east with his paints on a carrying pole, off to the southern hills to find 'a red for faces and a green for robes'. 'When the master says he'll find something, he'll spend his life finding it.'

name: 灯笼营
Lantern Camp
before: 偷粉本的货郎找到了：他如今发了点小财，雇了几个刀手当保镖，在路口扎了个营卖杂货。营门口挂着一只灯笼，糊灯笼的纸上有一张人脸的线条，针眼一排排的，灯一点，脸就在地上印出一圈光点。保镖们见有人盯着灯笼看，抽出了刀。

Here's the peddler who stole the patterns. He's done well for himself, hired swordsmen as bodyguards, and pitched a camp at the crossroads to sell sundries. A lantern hangs at the gate, papered with the outline of a face pricked full of holes, so that when it's lit the face is printed on the ground in points of light. The bodyguards see you staring at it and draw.
after: 保镖们跑了，货郎抱着头交代：那捆粉本三百页，他拆开卖了，糊灯笼的、包油饼的、纳鞋底的都有，剩下最厚的一沓，被几个戴金面的人一口价买走了。你们把灯笼摘下来，纸角写着「千里号·马夫小丁」。

The guards run and the peddler, hands over his head, confesses. He split up the three hundred sheets and sold them off: for lanterns, for wrapping oil cakes, for shoe soles. The thickest stack left was bought outright by men in golden masks. You take down the lantern. In the corner of the paper: 'Qianli caravan. Little Ding, groom.'

name: 千层底
Paper Soles
before: 一伙开小差的兵卒在路边歇脚，脚上的新布鞋纳得厚厚的，是从货郎那儿买来的。鞋底一层布一层纸，纸是厚实的好纸，走过沙地，竟在地上留下一串淡淡的人脸印子。兵卒们自己都没发觉，见你们追着他们的脚印看，以为是来抓逃兵的，拔刀就砍。

A band of deserters rests by the road in thick new cloth shoes bought from the peddler. The soles are layered cloth and paper, good stout paper, and across the sand they leave a faint trail of printed faces. The deserters haven't noticed. Seeing you follow their footprints, they take you for deserter-catchers and come at you swinging.
after: 兵卒们光着脚跑了，鞋留下了一堆。你们拆开鞋底，抽出三十多张粉本，有的被汗渍得模糊，有的还清清楚楚：一个大胡子，一个小个子，一个耳朵缺了一块的。每张纸角都有名字和编号。你们把它们晾在石头上，三十多张脸看着天。

The deserters flee barefoot and leave a heap of shoes. Unpicking the soles, you draw out more than thirty patterns, some blurred with sweat, some still crisp: a big beard, a little man, someone missing a piece of one ear. Each has a name and number in the corner. You lay them out to dry on the rocks, thirty-odd faces looking up at the sky.

name: 抬匣道
Casket Road
before: 一队金面刀卫抬着一口木匣赶路，走得很稳，生怕颠着。匣子上贴着封条：「第一百五十三号」。他们见有人过来，把匣子护在中间，刀出了鞘。领头的说：「匣里的东西，你们不配看。」

A troop of Gold Mask swordsmen carries a wooden casket along the road, stepping smoothly so as not to jolt it. The seal on it reads 'No. 153'. Seeing you, they close round the casket and unsheathe. 'What's in here,' says their leader, 'you aren't fit to see.'
after: 刀卫们败了，却没扔下匣子，抬着它退走了。领头的临走说了一句：「匣里是一个人的半张脸，洞主一片片找回来的，还缺一只眼睛。」原来每张脸都有一个号、一口匣，金面卫像收殓亲人那样，收拾着三百个人的脸。

Beaten, the swordsmen still don't drop the casket; they carry it off with them. Their leader says over his shoulder: 'Half a man's face. The Lord found it piece by piece. It's still missing an eye.' So every face has a number and a casket, and the Gold Masks gather up the three hundred faces the way a family gathers up its dead.

name: 补佛婆
The Statue Mender
before: 小村尽头一间屋，住着个补泥塑的老婆婆，专给缺了鼻子、掉了手指的佛像补泥。刮金帮的几个残兵找上门，逼她说出哪里还有贴金的佛，不说就砸她的泥盆。老婆婆把一团泥拍在桌上：「我只知道哪里的佛缺什么，不知道哪里的佛有金。」

At the end of a small village lives an old woman who mends clay Buddhas, patching on noses and fingers they've lost. Some Gold Scraper stragglers have come to make her tell them where gilded Buddhas are still to be found, or they'll smash her clay basins. She slaps a lump of clay on the table: 'I know what every Buddha is missing. I don't know which ones have gold.'
after: 刮金帮被赶走，老婆婆跟你们讲了金粉的来由：千里号的人画像时，非要往脸上调金，画匠劝都劝不住。账房说，窟里点灯的时候，三百张脸一齐亮起来，「回来的时候，一眼就认出谁是谁」。「是为了认人，不是为了富贵，」她叹口气，「偏偏招来了刮金的。」

Once the Scrapers are gone she tells you why there was gold at all. When the Qianli caravan were painted, they insisted on gold in their faces and the painter couldn't talk them out of it. The bookkeeper said that when the lamps were lit in the cave, all three hundred faces would shine at once, 'so when we come back, we'll know at a glance who's who'. 'It was for recognising each other, not for show,' she sighs. 'And it brought the scrapers.'

name: 胡麻油坊
Sesame Oil Mill
before: 路口一家胡麻油坊，榨油的石碾子转了几十年，香味飘出二里地。本地一个恶霸带着打手霸占了油坊，油价涨了三倍，连千佛洞点灯的油都要先给他交钱。他们卖的油饼用厚纸包着，纸上是一张张人脸，吃完的人顺手就扔在了地上。

A sesame oil mill at the crossroads, its millstone turning for decades and the smell carrying a mile. A local bully and his men have seized it and tripled the price of oil; even the lamp oil for the caves must pay him first. The oil cakes they sell come wrapped in thick paper printed with faces, and people toss the wrappers on the ground when they've eaten.
after: 恶霸被打跑，石碾子又咕噜噜转了起来。油坊老板把地上的包饼纸一张张捡回来，捋平了交给你们：都是粉本，被油浸得透亮，线条反倒更清楚了。他说以后包饼改用荷叶，「人家的脸，不能拿来包饼」。

With the bully run off, the millstone rumbles round again. The miller picks up the wrappers one by one, smooths them out and hands them to you: pounce patterns, soaked translucent with oil, the lines clearer than ever. From now on he'll wrap his cakes in lotus leaves. 'You don't wrap cakes in people's faces.'
first: 恶霸的库房里抄出二十坛胡麻油、半屋子芝麻饼、三十斤羊油、一口抢来的铜锅，还有一匣子他收的「过油税」，账上连千佛洞的老和尚都欠他一钱。

The bully's storeroom yields twenty jars of sesame oil, half a room of sesame cakes, thirty pounds of mutton fat, a stolen copper pot, and a box of his 'oil tax', whose ledger has even the old monk of the caves owing him a coin.
pass: 每次路过，油坊老板都给你们灌满一路的灯油，再塞一摞刚出锅的胡麻饼，用荷叶包着：「烫手，路上慢慢吃。」
Every time you pass, the miller fills your lamps for the road and presses on you a stack of sesame flatbreads fresh from the pan, wrapped in lotus leaves. 'Hot. Eat them slowly on the way.'

name: 揭壁营
Wall Peelers' Camp
before: 戈壁上一座大营，住着一伙盗壁贼，步卒、弩手、骑手都有。领头的是个关内来的巧手，会用湿布糊住壁画，等布干了一揭，整片画就连着泥皮下来了。他们正在营里试手，揭下来的飞天一块块堆在帐篷边。听说他们下一个要揭的，是一排没有脸的供养人。

A big camp of mural thieves on the gravel plain, foot, crossbow and horse. Their chief is a craftsman from inside the Pass who knows how to paste wet cloth over a painting and, when it dries, peel the whole thing off with the plaster attached. They're practising in camp, peeled apsaras stacked by the tents. Word is the next thing they'll peel is a row of donors with no faces.
after: 盗壁贼被打散，你们在领头的帐里搜出一张图，画的是千佛洞北崖，第三层一个窟口画了圈，旁边写着「千里窟，供养人三百身，脸已刮，身尚全，可揭」。图背面还有一行：「窟口有金面卫昼夜看守，须先引开。」那三百个没有脸的人，一直有人守着。

The thieves scattered, you find a map in the chief's tent: the north cliff of the caves, with a circle round one mouth on the third tier and the note 'Qianli Cave. Three hundred donors. Faces scraped, bodies intact. Can be peeled.' On the back: 'Gold Masks guard the mouth day and night. Must be lured away first.' Those three hundred faceless people have had someone watching over them all along.

name: 熬胶圈
The Glue Pen
before: 死胡同尽头一座羊圈，从前是画匠们熬胶的地方：皮子熬成胶，调进颜料，颜色才粘得住墙。如今一伙兵痞占了圈，把熬胶的大锅拿来炖羊肉，步、弩、骑一大帮，吃得满嘴流油。圈墙上钉着一块木板，写满了颜料的配方，被他们拿来当了砧板。

At the end of a dead-end track is a sheep pen where painters used to boil glue: hides rendered down and mixed into the paint, so the colour would hold to the wall. A big gang of soldier-thugs, foot, crossbow and horse, has taken it over and stews mutton in the glue cauldron, grease running down their chins. A board nailed to the wall, covered in paint recipes, has become their chopping block.
after: 兵痞被撵走，你们把那块砧板洗干净，配方还看得清：「人面：白土为底，土红晕颊，石绿描衣，墨点睛。金粉少许，调胶，灯下方见。」落款吴半壁。原来他要找的红和绿，都写在这块板子上。熬胶的老羊倌说，吴画匠临走前在这里熬了一锅胶，背走了。

The thugs driven off, you scrub the chopping block and the recipe still reads clearly: 'Faces: white earth for the ground, red earth for the cheeks, malachite green for robes, ink for the eyes. A little gold dust, mixed with glue, shows only by lamplight.' Signed Wu Banbi. The red and green he went looking for are both on this board. The old shepherd who boiled the glue says Wu cooked a whole pot here before he left and carried it off on his back.

name: 千佛小寺
Little Temple of a Thousand Buddhas
before: 路边小寺里住着个画僧，和吴画匠是一个师父教出来的。他在给小寺画一墙千佛，画了十年，才画到第六百个。一伙盗壁贼的探子赖在寺里，逼他画一张千佛洞北崖的窟图，他不肯，他们就把他的笔一支支掰断。

A painter-monk lives in a little roadside temple; he and Wu the painter learned from the same master. He has been painting a wall of a thousand Buddhas for ten years and has reached number six hundred. Scouts for the mural thieves have moved in and want him to draw them a plan of the north cliff. He refuses, so they are snapping his brushes one by one.
after: 探子被赶走了，画僧捡起断笔：「我画得慢，老吴画得快。他画脸，一张一刻钟，画得活。」他说老吴临走前来过，跟他借了一支最细的笔，说那三百张脸里最难画的是账房，「那人一双眼睛像在算你」。老吴画了三遍才画成。

The scouts run off and the monk picks up his broken brushes. 'I paint slowly. Old Wu paints fast. A face in a quarter of an hour, and alive.' Wu came by before he left, he says, to borrow his finest brush, and said the hardest of the three hundred faces was the bookkeeper's. 'The man's eyes look like they're working out what you're worth.' It took Wu three tries to get it.

name: 淘金滩
Panning Flats
before: 一片干河滩上蹲着几十个人，个个端着木盆淘沙，淘得满头大汗。他们听说千里号的金脸被刮下来以后，金粉让风吹到了戈壁上，就跑来淘，一淘三年。这片滩被淘金客的头子霸着，外人进来淘一盆要交一半。他们见你们走近，抄起了铁锹。

Dozens of people crouch on a dry riverbed with wooden pans, sifting sand and sweating. They heard that when the Qianli caravan's golden faces were scraped, the wind blew the gold dust out over the gravel plain, and they've been panning for it for three years. The flats belong to a panning boss who takes half of every pan an outsider washes. When you come near, they grab their shovels.
after: 淘金客散了，你们看看他们淘出来的东西：一小撮红的、绿的、白的颜料渣，夹着几粒亮闪闪的，倒真是金，可三年加起来还没有一粒米大。头子垂头丧气，说金粉早被金面卫的人一粒粒收走了，「他们比我们还会淘」。

With the panners dispersed, you look at what they've found: a pinch of red, green and white paint grit with a few bright specks, real gold, though three years' worth wouldn't make a grain of rice. Their boss hangs his head. The Gold Masks picked up the dust grain by grain long ago, he says. 'They're better panners than we are.'

name: 账房石
The Bookkeeper's Stone
before: 一块大石头上刻着一个人的半身像，线条简单：瘦脸，眯眼，耳朵后面夹着一支笔，手边一把算盘。一队金面刀卫奉命守着这块石头，不许人摸，不许人描，连放羊的都得绕着走。今天几个盗壁贼摸过来，想把它凿下来卖钱。

Carved on a boulder is a half-length portrait in a few plain lines: a thin face, narrowed eyes, a brush tucked behind one ear, an abacus at hand. A troop of Gold Mask swordsmen is under orders to guard it: no touching, no tracing, even shepherds must go round. Today a few mural thieves have crept up, meaning to chisel it off and sell it.
after: 盗壁贼和刀卫都退了，你们细看石像，石脚刻着一行小字：「吴半壁戏刻账房先生，丁未冬。」是画匠给账房画像之前，先拿石头练的手。刀卫头目临走说，洞主每月来看它一回，看完就走，一句话不说。三百张脸里，只有这一张没被刮掉。

Thieves and guards both gone, you study the stone. At its foot, small: 'Carved in jest by Wu Banbi: Master Bookkeeper. Winter, Dingwei year.' The painter warmed up on stone before he painted the man. The guard captain, leaving, says the Lord comes to look at it once a month, then goes without a word. Of all three hundred faces, this is the only one nobody scraped.

name: 面库
The Face Store
before: 死胡同里一座石砌的库房，门口站着金面卫最精的一队：刀卫、弩手、骑卫三路，个个面具擦得锃亮。库门上的封条一层盖一层，最新的一层是昨天的。库里不时传出纸张翻动的声音，像有人在里面一页页数着什么。

A stone storehouse at the end of a dead end, guarded by the best of the Gold Masks, sword, crossbow and horse, their masks polished bright. Seals cover the door layer on layer, the newest dated yesterday. From inside comes now and then a rustle of paper, as if someone is counting through something page by page.
after: 守库的人退走了，你们推开库门：三百口木匣码到房顶，每口一个号、一个名字。匣里是收回来的泥皮和粉本，有的快满了，有的只有指甲大一片，有的空着。翻纸声是风，从墙缝里吹进来。金面卫守的是三百个人的脸，一片一片，等它们凑齐。

The guards withdraw and you push open the door. Three hundred wooden caskets stand stacked to the ceiling, each with a number and a name. Inside are recovered flakes and patterns: some caskets nearly full, some holding one fingernail of plaster, some empty. The rustling was the wind through a crack in the wall. What the Gold Masks guard is three hundred faces, waiting piece by piece to be whole.

name: 刮金窝
The Scrapers' Den
before: 刮金帮的老窝藏在一道干沟尽头，当年刮过千里窟的那一伙就是从这里起家的。窝里聚着刮金帮最狠的一群，步、弩、骑都有，墙上挂着一排刷了金漆的纸面具，地上堆着竹片、刷子和一杆戥子。他们听说你们一路在问「三百张脸」，早早地等着了。

The Gold Scrapers' old den lies at the end of a dry gully; the gang that scraped the Qianli Cave got its start here. Their hardest members, foot, crossbow and horse, are gathered inside. On the wall hangs a row of paper masks painted gold; on the floor, bamboo slivers, brushes and a small steelyard for weighing gold. They've heard you've been asking about 'the three hundred faces' all along the road, and they're waiting.
after: 刮金帮被打垮了，戥子底下压着分赃的字据：「千里窟三百面，得金一钱二分，七人均分。」他们戴金漆纸面具吓唬守窟的和尚，月光照着金粉往外飘，放羊姑娘看成了下雪，缺牙老头记岔了月亮。字据末尾有朱笔批的四个字：「一人不漏。」笔迹和闭山令一样。

The Scrapers are broken, and under the steelyard lies their old share-out note: 'Qianli Cave, three hundred faces. Gold obtained: one tenth of an ounce and a little more. Split seven ways.' That night they wore gold-painted paper masks to frighten the monks guarding the cave. The moonlight caught the gold dust drifting out and the shepherd girl saw snow; the gap-toothed old man even got the moon wrong. At the bottom, in red ink: 'Not one escapes.' The hand is the same as on the order closing the mountain.

name: 试脸墙
The Trial Wall
before: 吴半壁带着凑齐的颜料，在一处土崖下抹了一面新墙，要先试画一张脸，「试成了，再去窟里补那三百张」。他刚把白土刷匀，一伙盗壁贼就围了上来：他们跟了一路，就等他把颜料凑齐。老头把颜料碟往怀里一揽，像抱着孙子。

With his colours finally gathered, Wu Banbi has plastered a fresh wall under an earth bank to try one face first. 'If it works, I'll go into the cave and do all three hundred.' He has barely brushed on the white ground when mural thieves close in; they've tailed him the whole way, waiting for him to complete his set. The old man gathers his paint dishes to his chest like a grandchild.
after: 盗壁贼被打散了，吴半壁洗了手，调胶，研色，一笔一笔地画。他先画的是账房：瘦脸，眯眼，耳后夹一支笔，眼睛像在算你。画完他退后三步看了很久：「颜色对了，就差金。」他说三百张脸他闭着眼都画得出，粉本只是给自己壮胆的。他托你们带句话给金面后头的人：「金子还回来，我就进窟。」墙上的账房看着你们，像是要开口报一个数。

The thieves scattered, Wu washes his hands, mixes glue, grinds pigment and paints stroke by stroke. He starts with the bookkeeper: thin face, narrowed eyes, brush behind the ear, eyes that seem to be reckoning you up. When it's done he steps back three paces and looks a long while. 'The colours are right. Only the gold is missing.' He could paint all three hundred with his eyes shut, he says; the patterns only gave him courage. He asks you to take a message to the man behind the golden mask: 'Give back the gold and I'll go into the cave.' The bookkeeper on the wall watches you as if about to name a figure.

name: 剃度坡
Tonsure Slope
before: 山脚的坡道上站着一排和尚，袈裟是新的，光头也是新的，头皮上还带着刮破的小口子。他们托着钵见人就拦：「施主，留下香火钱，佛祖保佑你平安过坡。」不给的，钵一扔，袖子里就掏出了短棍。其中一个和尚的后脑勺上，刺着「翠花」两个字。

A row of monks stands on the slope at the foot of the hills, new robes, new shaven heads still nicked from the razor. Alms bowls out, they stop everyone: 'Benefactor, leave an offering and the Buddha will see you safely over the slope.' Refuse, and the bowl drops and a cudgel comes out of a sleeve. One of them has a woman's name, Cuihua, tattooed on the back of his head.
after: 假和尚们被打得四散，落了一地度牒，个个盖着「金身寺」的大印，印泥还没干。被拦的香客告诉你们，这伙人今年春天才剃的头，占了千佛洞寺前的粥棚，粥从此要钱了。「那粥棚施了十年粥，从没收过一文。」

The false monks scatter and leave a litter of ordination papers, all stamped with the seal of the Golden Body Temple, the ink still wet. The pilgrims they'd stopped tell you this lot only shaved their heads this spring. They've taken over the porridge shed in front of the temple, and now the porridge costs money. 'Ten years that shed gave porridge away and never took a coin.'

name: 施粥碑
The Porridge Stele
before: 寺前的路边立着一块石碑，几个假和尚正抡着锤子凿碑上的字，凿得石屑乱飞，围观的香客敢怒不敢言。碑上的字已经凿掉了一半，剩下的还能认出「千里号」「施粥」「不取分文」几个字。凿碑的说，方丈有令：粥是金身寺的粥，跟什么千里号没关系。

By the road before the temple stands a stele, and false monks are hammering the inscription off it, stone chips flying, while pilgrims watch in silent fury. Half the text is gone already; you can still make out 'Qianli caravan', 'porridge' and 'free of charge'. The abbot's orders, say the chiselers: the porridge belongs to the Golden Body Temple and has nothing to do with any Qianli caravan.
after: 假和尚扔下锤子跑了，一个老香客拿手指摸着碑，把凿坏的字一个个念全了：「丁未冬，千里号三百人留粮三百石于寺前，施粥过客，不取分文。粮尽，自有人续。」「三百石粮，」老香客算了算，「顶多施三年。可这粥一施就是十年。」续粮的人是谁，碑上没写。

The false monks drop their hammers and run. An old pilgrim runs his fingers over the stele and reads out the damaged words: 'Winter of Dingwei. The three hundred of the Qianli caravan leave three hundred measures of grain before this temple, to give porridge to travellers free of charge. When the grain runs out, others will continue.' 'Three hundred measures,' the old man reckons. 'Three years at most. But the porridge has kept coming for ten.' Who kept it coming, the stele doesn't say.

name: 夜粮沟
Night Grain Gully
before: 附近的人都说，每年秋天，总有一辆粮车半夜出现在粥棚后面，车上满满的粮袋，赶车的却看不见人，天一亮车就没了。今年假和尚们得了信，在粥棚后面的沟里埋伏了一圈，就等着把这车粮截下来，拉回金身寺卖钱。月亮刚上来，远处传来了吱吱呀呀的车轮声。

People here say that every autumn a grain cart appears behind the porridge shed in the middle of the night, loaded with sacks, no driver to be seen, and is gone by dawn. This year the false monks got wind of it and have laid an ambush in the gully behind the shed to seize the grain and sell it at their temple. The moon has just risen, and in the distance a cart wheel creaks.
after: 假和尚们被打跑，粮车停在沟口，两头老牛自己站着，赶车的影子早已退回了黑处。每一只粮袋上都盖着一个红印，印的是一张没有五官的面具。你们把粮卸进了粥棚。老牛认得路，卸完粮，自己拉着空车往东北走了。

The false monks driven off, the cart stands at the mouth of the gully, its two old oxen waiting on their own; whoever drove it has already slipped back into the dark. Every sack is stamped in red with a mask that has no features. You unload the grain into the porridge shed. The oxen know the way. Once they're unloaded they haul the empty cart off to the north-east by themselves.

name: 千里粥棚
The Qianli Porridge Shed
before: 寺门前一座长棚，棚下十口大锅，从前每天天不亮就冒白气，过路的香客、驼夫、乞丐排着队喝粥。如今棚口坐着几个胖大和尚收钱，一钱一碗，粥稀得照得见人影。烧火的是个半聋的老火头，弓着背添柴，谁跟他说话，他都只会「啊？」

A long shed before the temple gate, ten great pots beneath it. Once they steamed every morning before dawn, and pilgrims, camel drivers and beggars queued for porridge. Now fat monks sit at the entrance taking a coin a bowl, and the porridge is thin enough to see your face in. The fire is tended by a half-deaf old cook, bent over the kindling, who answers everyone with 'Eh?'
after: 打到最后，假和尚的头目举棍冲上来，那老火头头也不回，反手一勺子敲在他脑门上，头目就躺下了。香客们这才知道，老火头年轻时是寺里的武僧，「耳朵不好，手可好」。十口大锅又冒起了稠稠的白气，那块「千里粥·不要钱」的旧木牌重新挂上了棚柱。

At the end the false monks' leader charges with his staff raised, and the old cook, without turning round, cracks him on the forehead with a ladle backhand. Down he goes. Only now do the pilgrims learn the old man was a fighting monk in his youth: 'Bad ears, good hands.' The ten pots steam thick and white again, and the old board, 'Qianli Porridge, Free', goes back up on the post.
first: 假和尚的库里抄出两袋白米（他们自己吃的）、四十坛腌萝卜、一箱收来的铜钱、一捆度牒，还有一箱假发髻：看来早就打算好了，捞够了就还俗。

The false monks' store gives up two sacks of white rice (for themselves), forty jars of pickled radish, a chest of collected coppers, a bundle of ordination papers, and a box of false topknots. They'd clearly planned to rejoin the world once they'd made their pile.
pass: 每次路过，老火头都给你们每人盛一碗稠粥，粥上卧一块腌萝卜，再包一大包锅巴让你们路上嚼，嘴里还是那句：「啊？不要钱！」

Every time you pass, the old cook ladles each of you a bowl of thick porridge with a piece of pickled radish on top and wraps up a big bundle of crispy rice crust for the road, still saying the same thing: 'Eh? It's free!'

name: 金身寺
Golden Body Temple
before: 山脚下一座大院，门匾上写着「金身寺」，可院墙是粮栈的墙，门口还留着拴牲口的石桩。大殿里供着一尊金身「活佛」，香客进来要先磕头再捐钱。护院的假和尚步、弩、骑都有，比真和尚多三倍。你们进殿的时候，那尊金身打了个喷嚏。

A big compound at the foot of the hills, 'Golden Body Temple' over the gate, though the walls are a grain merchant's walls and the hitching posts are still outside. In the hall sits a gilded 'living Buddha'; pilgrims must kowtow, then donate. The false monks guarding the place, foot, crossbow and horse, outnumber real monks three to one. As you enter the hall, the golden Buddha sneezes.
after: 假和尚们被冲散，「活佛」也顾不得端坐了，抹着脸上的金漆从后门跑了。他是金身寺的方丈，俗名钱满仓，原是关外的粮商，粮栈倒了才剃的头。大殿梁上藏着他的一张单子：「千里粥棚，每年秋有人续粮。粮从何来，查。」原来他占粥棚，图的是那个续粮的人。

The false monks routed, the 'living Buddha' abandons his pose and runs out the back, wiping gold paint off his face. He is the temple's abbot, born Qian Mancang, 'Granary-Full Qian', a grain merchant beyond the Pass who shaved his head when his business failed. Hidden on a beam in the hall is a note of his: 'Someone tops up the Qianli porridge shed every autumn. Find out where the grain comes from.' That's why he took the shed: he's after whoever sends the grain.

name: 典座寮
The Steward's Kitchen
before: 寺里管伙食的典座是个瘦高的老和尚，一辈子最恨糟蹋粮食，掉在地上一粒米也要捡起来吹吹吃了。假和尚占了他的厨房，逼他炖肉，他宁可饿着也不动刀，被锁进了柴房。厨房里，假和尚们吃剩的馒头扔得满地都是。

The temple steward, a tall thin old monk, has hated waste all his life; a grain of rice on the floor gets picked up, blown on and eaten. The false monks took his kitchen and ordered him to stew meat. He'd rather starve than lift a knife, so they locked him in the woodshed. In the kitchen, their half-eaten buns lie all over the floor.
after: 假和尚被撵走，典座出了柴房，先把地上的馒头一个个捡起来掸掉灰，才肯跟你们说话。他开了张，拿斋饭、豆子、干菜跟你们换东西，一文不多收。他说管粥棚的守粥师父两个月前上了山，去找续粮的人，「他徒弟豆子也跟着不见了」。

Once the false monks are gone the steward comes out of the woodshed and gathers up the buns one by one, dusting them off, and only then will he talk. He opens for business, trading the temple's vegetarian food, beans and dried greens, not a coin over the fair price. Master Shouzhou, who runs the porridge shed, went up the mountain two months ago, he says, to find whoever sends the grain. 'And his novice, Douzi, has gone missing too.'

name: 香灰窑
The Incense Kilns
before: 山脚的一排窑洞冒着黑烟，假和尚们在这里做香：锯末掺牛粪，搓成条，晒干了刷一层红，就是「千佛洞开光香」，一捆卖二十钱。窑口守着一大帮打手，步、弩、骑都有，谁靠近就说是「偷佛门秘方」。香客买回去一点，熏得直流眼泪，还以为是佛祖显灵。

A row of kiln caves at the foot of the hill belches black smoke. The false monks make incense here: sawdust and cow dung rolled into sticks, dried, painted red, and sold as 'Consecrated Incense of the Thousand Buddha Caves' at twenty coins a bundle. A big crowd of toughs, foot, crossbow and horse, guards the kilns, and anyone who comes close is 'stealing the temple's secret recipe'. Pilgrims light it at home, weep from the smoke, and take it for a miracle.
after: 打手们被打散，你们在窑里翻出钱满仓给手下的一封信：「香钱照收。另，续粮之人必从山上来，盯住守粥那个胖和尚，他知道。」窑工们说，守粥师父从不买他们的香，只在粥棚里点一盏清油灯，「他说佛不缺香，人缺粥」。

The toughs scattered, you turn up a letter from Qian Mancang to his men in the kilns: 'Keep taking the incense money. Also: whoever sends the grain must come down from the mountain. Watch that fat monk Shouzhou. He knows.' The kiln workers say Master Shouzhou never bought their incense; he only lit a plain oil lamp in the porridge shed. 'He said the Buddha doesn't lack incense. People lack porridge.'
